basis: Colobomatous microphthalmia, hypogonadism and intellectual disability define the syndrome; each is reported in 30-79%.

Renal agenesis/hypodysplasia defines disease. Pulmonary hypoplasia occurs in 2/3 and fixed clubfoot deformity in 3/3 reported patients.
Congenital peripheral neuropathy and multiple congenital joint contractures define the syndrome.
Disseminated tuberculosis with characteristic pulmonary lesions; hepatic granulomatous inflammation with biochemical dysfunction occurs in roughly half.
Inherited progressive degeneration of the nervous system; additional organ involvement is subtype dependent.
Developmental disability, hypotonia and seizures define disease. Joint hypermobility alone does not establish joint damage; structural organ defects are uncommon.
Progressive skeletal muscular dystrophy and dilated cardiomyopathy are defining manifestations in the definition and syndromic synonym.
Neurodevelopmental syndrome; supplied HPO reports hydronephrosis, heart malformation and gut dysmotility at 80-99%. Skeletal defects and ptosis omitted by cap.
Isolated bilateral cerebellar hypoplasia causes motor, cognitive and language deficits; no additional organ disorder is defined.
Benign bone-forming neoplasm, including osteoma, osteoid osteoma and osteoblastoma.
Mitochondrial metabolic disease with marrow failure and exocrine pancreatic dysfunction. Hepatic failure 3/5; renal, cardiac, neurologic and ocular involvement omitted by cap.
Intellectual disability defines disease. Alopecia 80-99%; skeletal malformations include pectus excavatum and cubitus valgus (2/2 each); strabismus 11/29 (~38%).
Primary ovarian endocrine failure with low estradiol and elevated gonadotropins; gonads as hormone organs belong to metabolic_endocrine.
Autoimmune destruction of blood platelets defines the condition.
Colobomatous microphthalmia and intellectual disability define disease; kyphoscoliosis occurs in 4/4 reported patients.
Benign neoplasm occupying the spleen, included in the haematologic axis; benign neoplasia alone is not an immune mechanism.
Cardiomyopathy and hearing loss define the condition. Associated myopathy and ataxia lack evidence of frequency at or above 30%.
Interpreted as an erythrocyte T-antigen anomaly; definition and phenotype evidence are absent, so no additional organs assigned.
Elevated intraocular pressure is an eye disorder; the hypertension ancestor does not establish cardiovascular disease.
Tuberculous infection directly involves brain, meninges or spinal cord; other sites are not required by this concept.
Hydrocele involves the male reproductive compartment, outside the axes; infection is confined to a separate subtype.
The syndrome is defined by shoulder girdle structural defects and familial intellectual disability; no additional phenotype evidence supplied.
Inherited high myopia affects the eye. Retinal detachment occurs in only 1/9 and remains within the same ocular axis.
